subject: telescope
reasoning:
I need a root joint since the builder requires one even for non-creature props. I'm planning a classic refractor telescope on a tripod with an alt-az mount, roughly a 1-meter tube on a 1.2-meter tripod, keeping the joint hierarchy simple while still looking realistic.

I'm sketching the structure: three tripod legs with tapered rods and small feet, a mount head with azimuth and altitude joints, and the optical tube attached to the altitude joint tilted up about 25 degrees so it moves naturally as a child of that joint.

For the tube itself, I'm placing the main barrel along the z-axis in navy/cream, adding a wider dew shield with a dark lens disc at the front, and a brass focuser with an eyepiece tube at the back.

Also sketching a small finder scope mounted above the tube on rings and brackets, brass lathe-ring bands wrapping around the tube at intervals, and a pivot hub cylinder at the alt axis with knobs on both sides for the cradle.

I'm designing the fork assembly with a tapered post and cheek plates that cradle the tube, sized so it fits with clearance, rotating around the alt joint hub. Then I'm placing the tripod head and figuring out foot positions spaced 120° apart at a fixed radius from the head.

Each leg will be built from two rod segments, a thicker upper and thinner lower, joined by a small clamp ring capsule at midpoint, ending in a rubber-capped spike foot resting near the ground.

For the spreader tray, I'm positioning it at around y=0.55 where the leg radius works out to roughly 0.325, using a lathed triangular cross-section to form a three-sided tray, and considering adding small brass eyepiece cylinders on top as a decorative detail.

Rather than floating the tray disconnected, I'm linking it to the legs with spider-arm rods running from a center point out to each leg at tray height, plus a small central disc holding the eyepieces. I'm also setting up the joint hierarchy -- root, azimuth axis, altitude axis -- and defining how each part attaches to its parent bone before posing the altitude joint at -25 degrees, then starting on the lathed profile for the telescope head mount.

Checking for collisions, I notice the tube bottom overlaps slightly with the crossbar, so I'm lowering the crossbar's position and shortening the post height to keep everything clear.

Now I'm placing the hub knobs using mirrored lathe shapes along the x-axis, adding focus knobs on the focuser near the tube's back, and positioning the finder scope slightly above the tube at y=1.61.

I'm sketching the finder's rods, rings, and brackets with small radii, plus a brass objective ring and eyepiece rod. I'm also setting the color palette—cream tube, brass trim, navy accents, black, wood tones, and lens blue—before writing a helper function to generate ring shapes along the z-axis for the lathe geometry.

Now I'm figuring out the dew shield and lens placement, making the shield a hollow lathed tube instead of a solid rod to avoid z-fighting, and positioning the lens disc so it protrudes slightly beyond the tube's front end for a more realistic look.

Setting rod caps to flat and bumping sides to 16 for smoother tubes, then I'll build the leg rods from head to feet using a root bone before writing everything out.
